thm:direct-sum-firewall.title: Direct-sum firewall
thm:direct-sum-firewall.note: Proved: any PSD blocks assemble to a PSD direct sum (including a singular or zero second block), the compression to the first summand equals T1 exactly, and it is independent of the second block - so a coercive statement about one typed block constrains nothing about the other without an intertwining theorem.

prop:old-abel.title: Abel reduction
prop:old-abel.note: Proved: for Re s > 0 and absolutely summable weighted coefficients (Summable ||c(n)|| n^{-Re s}), int_1^infty (sum_{n<=x} c(n)) x^{-s-1} dx = (1/s) sum_n c(n) n^{-s}, by dominated tsum/integral interchange with per-n tail evaluation int_n^infty x^{-s-1} dx = n^{-s}/s. The manuscript states only s != 0 on the vertical line; the formal statement carries Re s > 0 as hypothesis, which is the regime where the tail integrals converge absolutely and is the regime the corollary uses. The displayed shifted-product instance c(n) = a_i(n) a_j(n+h) is NCG.abel_reduction_shifted (nonnegative shift h; negative shifts relabel the two ports).

cor:old-zero.title: The zero-shift slice is not an $L$-function frame
cor:old-zero.note: Proved: the zero-shift slice with a_i = Lambda rho_i has Dirichlet coefficient Lambda(n)^2 rho_i(n) rho_j(n) -- a squared, unconjugated von Mangoldt weight, formalized as the identity int_1^infty A(x) x^{-s-1} dx = (1/s) sum_n Lambda(n)^2 rho_i(n) rho_j(n) n^{-s} for Re s > 0. The manuscript sentences observing that this weight is neither an L-function coefficient sequence nor of the form -L'/L (no Euler product / no single-prime support) are interpretive prose about the displayed formula and are not separately formalized.

thm:finite-weil.title: Finite reflected Weil criterion
thm:finite-weil.note: Proved: for a finite multiset Z invariant with multiplicity under the reflection R rho = 1 - conj(rho) (hypothesis Z.map R = Z), every point of Z lies on Re s = 1/2 iff the reflected Weil form W_Z[u] = sum_rho u(rho) conj(u(R rho)) is nonnegative (in the complex order, i.e. real and >= 0) for every polynomial u. The failure direction constructs the Lagrange interpolating polynomial equal to 1 at an off-line point, -1 at its reflection, and 0 at all other distinct points, making the form equal to -(m + m') < 0 (the manuscript -2m, with the two multiplicities equal by invariance).

corollary:ordinary-frames-do-not-locate-.title: Ordinary frames do not locate zeros
corollary:ordinary-frames-do-not-locate-.note: Proved: the unreflected energy sum_rho |u(rho)|^2 is nonnegative for every zero configuration and positive whenever u does not annihilate Z (formalized with the positivity witness as hypothesis). The closing sentence -- that horizontal information enters only through the reflected cross-pairing -- is interpretive prose contrasting with thm:finite-weil.

lem:laplace-pole.title: Laplace-pole obstruction
lem:laplace-pole.note: Proved with the manuscript's pole contradiction made quantitative and elementary, with the rendering disclosed. The Laplace transform is tested at z = lambda_k + eps: the weighted-energy hypothesis int e^{-2 sigma r}|f|^2 < infty bounds |Lf(z)| uniformly in eps (an AM-GM splitting ||f|| e^{-(sigma+a+eps)r} <= (e^{-2 sigma r}||f||^2 + e^{-2(a+eps)r})/2 replaces Cauchy-Schwarz); termwise integration of the exponential series is justified by summability of the norm integrals (integral_tsum_of_summable_integral_norm) since every exponent is dominated by Re lambda_k; each term integrates exactly to c_j/(z - lambda_j) (integral_exp_mul_complex_Ioi); the isolated k-term contributes |c_k|/eps while the separated tail is bounded by (2/delta) sum|c_j|; taking eps small enough makes |c_k|/eps exceed every bound, the contradiction. Disclosed hypotheses standing in for the manuscript's setting: the tested exponent is isolated (hsep; 'equal exponents grouped' over a discrete zero set) and of maximal real part (hmax; the rightmost pole is the one tested, matching the rightmost-displacement reduction in thm:gaussian-grh), and the entire Laplace transform of the remainder R enters through its local integrability and boundedness near lambda_k (hR). No complex-analytic continuation is needed in this rendering; the conclusion Re lambda_k <= sigma is the lemma's displayed bound.

thm:gaussian-grh.title: Gaussian Hardy criterion for GRH
thm:gaussian-grh.note: All three clauses, with the explicit-formula inputs disclosed. (i) gaussian_energy_finite: if sigma exceeds every displacement (Theta < sigma, 0 < sigma), the packet f = R + sum c_rho e^{lambda_rho r} is dominated pointwise by C_R + S e^{Theta' r} with S = sum |c_rho| < infty (termwise tsum bound), and e^{-2 sigma r}|f|^2 is dominated by two integrable exponentials - the energy is finite. (ii) is exactly the Laplace-pole obstruction of the lem:laplace-pole record (laplace_pole_obstruction): finite energy forces Re lambda <= sigma at the tested rightmost isolated exponent; the reflection symmetry rho -> 1 - conj(rho) (lambda -> -conj(lambda)) applies the same bound on the reflected exponent, giving the two-sided bound |Re rho - 1/2| <= sigma as in the manuscript. (iii) gaussian_grh_criterion: a displacement bounded by every positive sigma on both reflection sides vanishes - finiteness of the energy for every sigma > 0 is therefore equivalent to all displacements being zero, the Hardy criterion. Disclosed: the Gaussian specialization of the explicit formula (grouped absolutely summable coefficients, remainder with entire transform, reflection symmetry of the zero set) enters as the shared displayed hypotheses; the principal-channel pole clearing is prose.

thm:plancherel.title: Exact Gaussian Plancherel identity
thm:plancherel.note: Proved: for the cutoff-matched Gaussian port G^tri(r) = e^{i tau r} int e^{-(1/2+i tau)u} G_A(u-r) d e^tri(u) (NCG.gaussPort, with the arithmetic measure sum_{n<=X} chi(n) Lambda(n) delta_{log n} - delta_chi 1_{(0,log X]} e^u du written out as the atomic sum plus windowed integral, chi a Dirichlet character and Lambda the von Mangoldt function) and the cutoff transform L^tri(s) (NCG.cutoffL), the exact identity int e^{-2 sigma r} |G^tri(r)|^2 dr = (e^{2A sigma^2}/2pi) int e^{-2A(t-tau)^2} |L^tri(1/2+sigma+it)|^2 dt holds for every real sigma. Proof exactly as in the manuscript: the complex-shift Gaussian transform int e^{zr} G_A(u-r) dr = e^{zu} e^{Az^2} (NCG.gaussian_shift, from integral_cexp_quadratic), the pointwise transform formula hat h(t) = e^{A(-sigma+i(tau-t))^2} L^tri(1/2+sigma+it) (NCG.port_transform, atomic terms + Fubini for the windowed continuous part), the L^2 Plancherel theorem through the L^1-cap-L^2 Fourier bridge of the mass-flux file, and the scaling substitution t = 2 pi xi matching the manuscript unitary convention.

thm:residue-parseval.title: Character--residue Parseval identity
thm:residue-parseval.note: Proved for packets v : (ZMod q)^x -> H in an arbitrary complex inner-product space H: with vbar = (q-1)^{-1} sum_a v_a and G_chi = sum_a chi(a) v_a, sum_a ||v_a - vbar||^2 = (q-1)^{-1} sum_{chi != chi_0} ||G_chi||^2 (NCG.residue_parseval_prime, prime modulus as displayed; NCG.residue_parseval is the general-modulus version with phi(n) in place of q-1). The proof is the finite character Plancherel identity (DirichletCharacter orthogonality) with the principal channel subtracted, exactly as in the manuscript. The specific weighted Gaussian port space H_sigma and prime packets v_a are instances of the abstract H and v.

prop:v002-imprimitive.note: Induction rendered by Mathlib DirichletCharacter.changeLevel along q | Q. Zeros of added factors proved to lie on Re s = 0 (|chi*(p)| = 1), and the strip-zero identification L(s,chi) = 0 iff L(s,chi*) = 0 for Re s > 0 is proved; the multiplicity refinement (analytic order) is subsumed by the exact identity and is not separately formalized. thm:v002-twisted-mellin.title: Exact twisted Mellin transform
thm:v002-twisted-mellin.note: Boxed identity proved for continuous compactly supported C and Re s > 1/2, with delta as an explicit parameter of the centered packet (the identity is linear in delta; the prose convention delta_chi = 1 exactly in the primitive trivial channel is definitional). -L'/L(s+1/2, chi) is rendered as the logarithmic derivative of the Dirichlet L-series via Mathlib LSeries_twist_vonMangoldt_eq (Re(s+1/2) > 1, the series domain). Absolute convergence is established, not assumed: the substitution u = log(a/X) is carried out by an explicit exp change of variables, the prime side by countable Fubini (integral_tsum_of_summable_integral_norm plus a proved integrable-tsum companion), the centered channel by product-measure Fubini with the tail integral int_1^infty y^{-s-1/2} dy = 1/(s-1/2) computed by FTC. C smooth is weakened to C continuous with compact support (strictly more general).

thm:v002-zero-amplification.title: Off-critical zero amplification
thm:v002-zero-amplification.note: Proved in the boundedness rendering of the boxed limsup, with the continuation route replaced by the equivalent elementary Laplace-pole test (disclosed). In the logarithmic variable r = log X, an off-critical zero contributes the exponential c_k e^{lambda_k r} with alpha = Re lambda_k > 0 and grouped residue c_k = -m_rho H_C(rho - 1/2) != 0. If the packet satisfied |E(X)| <= C X^{alpha - eps} (i.e. |f(r)| <= C e^{(alpha-eps)r}), its weighted energy at sigma = alpha - eps/2 would be finite (the integrand is dominated by C^2 e^{-eps r}), and laplace_pole_obstruction would force alpha <= alpha - eps/2 - contradiction. Hence no such bound holds for any eps > 0: the boxed limsup |E|/X^{alpha-eps} = infinity in its unboundedness rendering. Disclosed: the tested exponent is the isolated rightmost one (the manuscript's displacement-maximal pole), the remainder transform is locally bounded near it (hR), and the completed-packet variant (holomorphic conductor-Gamma term at rho) is the manuscript's prose remark.

thm:v002-packet-grh.title: Packetwise conditional GRH

Hence SP(chi) forces every tested zero exponent into Re <= 0: the right half of the strip is zero-free. Disclosed: the reflection of left-half zeros into the conjugate primitive channel through the typed functional equation, and the primitive-to-imprimitive extension concluding full Dirichlet GRH from all primitive channels, are the manuscript's prose steps (their records thm:v002-functional-equation and corollary:primitive-reduction-of-dirichlet-grh are separate ledger items).

prop:v002-translation-nogo.title: Finite self-translation no-go

Construction as in the manuscript: Lagrange interpolation of logarithm branches, F = P e^h. The concluding sentence that finite translated lower frames therefore do not constrain horizontal zero positions is interpretive prose.

thm:v002-hurwitz-rh.title: Real-rooted approximation implies RH
thm:v002-hurwitz-rh.note: Proved with Hurwitz's dichotomy as a displayed hypothesis (disclosed). The manuscript's argument is carried out in full: if Xi had a nonreal zero z0, the closed ball of radius |Im z0|/2 around z0 avoids the real axis (|Im z - Im z0| <= |z - z0| pointwise), so every D_n is zero-free there because its zeros are all real; Hurwitz's dichotomy (hHurwitz: a locally uniform limit of zero-free holomorphic functions on a ball is zero-free or identically zero there) then either contradicts Xi(z0) = 0 directly or forces Xi = 0 on the ball, and the identity theorem for the entire function Xi (AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero on the connected plane) propagates this to Xi = 0 everywhere, contradicting Xi not identically zero. Hurwitz's theorem itself is the single standard cited input (no argument-principle/Rouche machinery exists in Mathlib yet); the disk selection, zero-freeness transfer, and identity-theorem branch are fully formal. Conclusion rendered as: every zero of Xi is real (Im = 0), the manuscript's RH equivalence.

thm:v003-twinfree-marginals.title: Twin-free realization of all sub-half marginals
thm:v003-twinfree-marginals.note: Proved: for any admissible tuple h : Fin k -> Z and marginals 0 <= pi_i <= 1/2 there is an explicit probability distribution on subsets of coordinates (nonnegative, total mass one) supported on independent sets of the twin graph G_2(H) (edges |h_i - h_j| = 2) with vertex marginals exactly pi_i. Construction as in the manuscript: mod-4 bipartition ({0,1} vs {2,3} residues), a fair coin for the side, then independent inclusion with probability 2 pi_i on the chosen side. The closing sentence that no linear functional of one-coordinate marginals can certify a twin edge is interpretive prose about this construction.

prop:v003-maynard-ceiling.title: Maynard coordinate ceiling

NCG.maynard_ceiling substitutes J <= I into the standard first-moment asymptotic pi_i = (log R/log N) J/I + o(1), R = N^{theta/2-delta} (taken as hypothesis: it is the external Maynard input), and yields convergence of the marginals to a limit <= theta/2 - delta < 1/2 -- inside the twin-free regime of NCG.twinfree_marginals, which is the compatibility assertion.

lem:fourier-boundary.title: Fourier boundary identity
lem:fourier-boundary.note: Proved for Hilbert-valued coefficients and monotone cell centres s_0 <= ... <= s_N: with the step prefix field J_d = q_c on [s_c, s_{c+1}) (NCG.stepPrefix), sum_c e^{it s_c} d_c = e^{it s_N} M(d) - it int e^{its} J_d(s) ds for every real t (NCG.fourier_boundary; the identity is stated in multiplied-by-it form, so no t != 0 restriction is needed). NCG.fourier_boundary_unitary is the boxed display with the unitary transform hat J(t) = (2 pi)^{-1/2} int e^{its} J(s) ds, which is defined in-file (NCG.unitaryHat) with exactly that normalization.

thm:mass-flux.title: Mass--flux inequality
thm:mass-flux.note: Proved: with the tensor packet C_F(d) realized as the H-valued L^2 function u -> sum_c F(u+s_c) d_c (NCG.portSynthesis, the canonical H (x) L^2 = L^2(R,H) picture), monotone cells, and F in L^1 cap L^2, ||C_F(d)|| <= ||F|| ||M(d)|| + sqrt(Lambda) ||J_d|| in L^2 (NCG.mass_flux), where Lambda = sup (2 pi xi)^2 |fourier F(xi)|^2 equals 2 pi Lambda_F in the manuscript unitary convention (statement in Mathlib Fourier convention; hypothesis Lambda as a pointwise bound). When M(d) = 0, the exact flux identity ||C_F(d)||^2 = int (2 pi xi)^2 |fourier F|^2 ||fourier J(-xi)||^2 d xi holds (NCG.mass_flux_zero; equal to the boxed display by Plancherel on J). The proof runs through a new L^1 cap L^2 compatibility bridge for the Mathlib vector-valued L^2 Fourier isometry (NCG.fourier_toLp_eq, multiplication formula + Schwartz density), the mass-prefix boundary identity, and the L^2 triangle inequality after the exact A+B frequency split. In the manuscript's unitary convention the envelope carries the factor 2 pi (cf. the thm:mass-flux ledger note), so the constant reads 2 pi/(2 a e) = pi/(a e) - the boxed pi/(a e) (disclosed).
